itineraries.title: Red, White & Raleigh: A Downtown Fourth
itineraries.theme: A free, all-American downtown day capped by fireworks at Dix Park
itineraries.drive_time: Everything within ~10 min of downtown; free Dix shuttle from Moore Square
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$40 (all events free; spend is food + parking)
itineraries.overview: Raleigh goes all-in on America's 250th: a morning parade, the free Capitol 250 Freedom Fest with historic interpreters and a reading of the Declaration, indoor play at Marbles when the heat peaks, then the city's big fireworks show on the Big Field at Dorothea Dix Park. It's a 103°F scorcher — hydrate hard and bank an air-conditioned break midday.

morning.title: First in Freedom July 4th Parade
morning.notes: Stake out shade on Fayetteville St before the sun climbs.

morning.title: Capitol 250: North Carolina Freedom Fest
morning.location: North Carolina State Capitol, 1 E Edenton St, Raleigh, NC 27601
morning.notes: Live music, historic interpreters, hands-on activities and a reading of the Declaration of Independence on the Capitol grounds.

afternoon.title: Independence Day Play at Marbles
afternoon.location: Marbles Kids Museum, 201 E Hargett St, Raleigh, NC 27601
afternoon.notes: Air-conditioned midday reset for families — fizzing 'fireworks' and water play. Adults can duck into the NC Museum of Natural Sciences (free) instead.

evening.title: Raleigh Fourth of July Fireworks at Dix Park
evening.location: Dorothea Dix Park, 2105 Umstead Dr, Raleigh, NC 27603
evening.notes: Gates 6 PM, music and food trucks, fireworks ~9:30 PM. Take the free Moore Square shuttle; no alcohol permitted on the Big Field.

food.vegan_dish: Avocado toast (no cheese) with a cold brew
food.notes: Fayetteville St coffeehouse, opens early — fuel before the parade.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan Southern fried 'chicken' & waffles
food.notes: Fully vegetarian/vegan on W Martin St; reserve ahead on the holiday.

food.vegan_dish: Loaded veggie taco or falafel wrap from a lot vendor
food.notes: Eat on-site so you don't lose your fireworks spot.

alternatives.good_weather: Blanket on the Big Field for the full show
alternatives.rain: If afternoon storms roll through, watch for the city's rain call on raleighnc.gov and pivot to an indoor rooftop view downtown.
Move the Marbles / Natural Sciences stop earlier and stay indoors.

practical_notes: 103°F and full sun — bring more water than you think, wear a hat, take a midday AC break.
Park once in a downtown deck (Wilmington/Blount) and use the free Dix shuttle from Moore Square in the evening.
Dix Park fills early for fireworks; arrive by 7:30 PM for a good lawn spot.

itineraries.title: Bull City Fourth: Market, Parade & Ballpark Fireworks
itineraries.theme: A classic Durham Independence Day from farmers market to a Bulls fireworks night
itineraries.drive_time: All within ~10 min around downtown Durham
itineraries.overview: Start at the Durham Farmers' Market under the Central Park pavilion, join the kids' bike-and-wagon parade, graze the free BullCity Freedom & Good Food Fest all afternoon, then close the night with Triple-A baseball and a post-game fireworks show as the Durham Bulls host the Gwinnett Stripers. A rooftop party is the grown-up alternative to the ballpark.

morning.title: Durham Farmers' Market
morning.location: Pavilion at Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham, NC 27701
morning.notes: Peaches, pastries and cold brew before the heat; producer-only, 8am–12pm.

morning.title: Children's Independence Day Parade
morning.location: Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham, NC 27701
morning.notes: Decorate a bike or wagon (materials provided); parade steps off ~10:30 AM, then popsicles and fire-truck tours.

afternoon.title: BullCity Freedom and Good Food Fest
afternoon.location: Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham, NC 27701
afternoon.notes: Live music, DJs, food trucks and kids' activities right in Central Park.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs. Gwinnett Stripers + Fireworks
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham, NC 27701
evening.notes: First pitch 6:45 PM with a July 4th post-game fireworks show. Buy ahead — holiday games sell out.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan glazed donut + tofu scramble biscuit
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg & cheese on a house biscuit
food.notes: A block from Central Park; grab-and-go before the market.

food.vegan_dish: Falafel wrap or veggie arepa from a Central Park truck
food.notes: Build lunch from the market and fest vendors.

food.vegan_dish: Marinara pie, hold the cheese, add roasted vegetables
food.notes: Downtown on Main St, near the ballpark; wood-fired, seasonal. Or eat at the park.

alternatives.good_weather: Ballpark seats for the game + fireworks
alternatives.rain: If the game is delayed, head to The Roof at The Durham Hotel rooftop party for downtown views and a DJ.
Shelter under the market pavilion or slip into a Foster St café until the storm clears.

practical_notes: Very hot and sunny (~103°F) — shade at Central Park is limited midday; hydrate.
Downtown decks (Chapel Hill St / Corcoran) put you within a walk of the market, park and ballpark.
Bulls July 4 fireworks games routinely sell out; secure tickets in advance.

itineraries.title: Carrboro to Chapel Hill: A People's Parade & a Drone Show
itineraries.theme: A community-minded Fourth with a hometown parade and a 300-drone finale
itineraries.drive_time: Carrboro and Chapel Hill are ~5–10 min apart
itineraries.overview: Carrboro does the Fourth its own way: morning at the Carrboro Farmers' Market, the beloved People's Parade led by the Bulltown Strutters, and a Town Commons celebration. Cool off in the afternoon, then head to Chapel Hill High for the town's free 300-drone light show (replacing fireworks). Night owls can catch nerdcore rapper MC Chris in the Cat's Cradle Back Room.

morning.title: Carrboro Farmers' Market
morning.location: Carrboro Town Commons, 301 W Main St, Carrboro, NC 27510
morning.notes: One of NC's best markets; go early (7am–12pm) before the heat.

morning.title: Carrboro's People's Parade & Town Commons
morning.location: Weaver Street Market / Carrboro Town Hall, 101 E Weaver St, Carrboro, NC 27510
morning.notes: Decorate a bike, march in the 10:50 AM People's Parade, then Town Commons festivities and an afternoon community reading.

afternoon.title: Beat-the-heat break at Weaver Street / Ackland
afternoon.location: Weaver Street Market lawn or Ackland Art Museum, Chapel Hill
afternoon.notes: Shade and AC — the Ackland's galleries are free and open; grab an iced coffee on the Weaver St lawn.

evening.title: Chapel Hill Fourth of July Drone Show
evening.location: Chapel Hill High School, 9217 Seawell School Road, Chapel Hill, NC 27516
evening.notes: Food vendors from 7 PM, ~300-drone light show around 9:20 PM. Free parking with shuttles.

evening.title: MC Chris at Cat's Cradle Back Room (optional)
evening.location: Cat's Cradle (Back Room), 300 E Main St, Carrboro, NC 27510
evening.notes: Nerdcore late-night in Carrboro if you'd rather trade the drone show for a club set.

food.vegan_dish: Tofu scramble + vegan pastry from the bakery
food.notes: Co-op market right on the Town Commons — perfect market-morning fuel.

food.vegan_dish: Falafel plate with hummus, tabbouleh and baba ghanoush
food.notes: Franklin St institution with a huge veg/vegan hot bar.

food.vegan_dish: Chana masala with brown rice
food.notes: Clearly labeled vegan dishes; community-minded spot off Franklin St.

alternatives.good_weather: Lawn seating at Chapel Hill High
alternatives.rain: Storms can scrub a drone show — check @chapelhillgov before heading out; fall back to MC Chris indoors at Cat's Cradle.
Ackland Art Museum and Weaver Street's indoor seating stay dry.

practical_notes: Hot and sunny (~103°F); the market and parade are shade-limited — hydrate and start early.
Park once in Carrboro and walk to the market/parade; drive to Chapel Hill High for the evening (use the free shuttles).
The drone show replaces fireworks — great for noise-sensitive kids and pets.

itineraries.title: Cary's Symphony & Sparks at Koka Booth
itineraries.theme: A polished, family-friendly Fourth with the NC Symphony and lakeside fireworks
itineraries.drive_time: Koka Booth is ~20 min from Raleigh; ~10 min around Cary/Morrisville
itineraries.overview: Cary's Independence Day is the Triangle's most polished: a free lawn show at Koka Booth Amphitheatre with the North Carolina Symphony and Cary Town Band, kids' activities, and a fireworks finale over Symphony Lake. Warm up with a morning at the Western Wake Farmers Market and downtown Cary before the gates open at 3:30 PM.

morning.title: Western Wake Farmers Market
morning.location: Indian Creek Trailhead Park, 101 Town Hall Dr, Morrisville, NC 27560
morning.notes: Producer-focused Morrisville market (8am–12pm); grab breakfast and picnic supplies for the lawn.

afternoon.title: Cary Independence Day Celebration — gates open
afternoon.location: Koka Booth Amphitheatre, 8003 Regency Parkway, Cary, NC 27518
afternoon.notes: Stake out lawn space early; kids' zone and Cary Town Band in the afternoon.

evening.title: NC Symphony + Fireworks over Symphony Lake
evening.location: Koka Booth Amphitheatre, 8003 Regency Parkway, Cary, NC 27518
evening.notes: Patriotic program by the NC Symphony, fireworks finale ~9:25 PM over the lake.

food.place: Once in a Blue Moon Bakery
food.vegan_dish: Fruit & a vegan muffin
food.notes: Downtown Cary bakery-café near the market.

food.vegan_dish: Falafel platter with hummus and tabbouleh
food.notes: Quick Mediterranean lunch before heading to Koka Booth.

food.vegan_dish: Veggie kebab or falafel wrap from a lot vendor
food.notes: Outside food/coolers policy varies — check boothamphitheatre.com before packing a picnic.

alternatives.good_weather: Blanket + low chairs on the lawn
alternatives.rain: The show runs rain-or-shine for music, but fireworks can be delayed — watch the Town of Cary channels for updates.

alternatives.good_weather: Stroll Downtown Cary Park's splash features
alternatives.rain: Shift the market run earlier and browse downtown Cary shops.

practical_notes: Very hot (~103°F): the lawn bakes in afternoon sun — bring a canopy or umbrella, sunscreen and water.
Arrive by mid-afternoon for lawn space and easier parking; expect a slow exit after fireworks.
Reserved table seats are limited and ticketed; the lawn is free general admission.

itineraries.title: Beat the Crowds: Fireworks on the Third
itineraries.theme: Get your fireworks fix a night early across the western suburbs
itineraries.drive_time: Apex, Cary and Garner are all 10–20 min apart
itineraries.overview: Skip the July 4 crush and celebrate on the third: several Triangle towns light up a night early. Apex's Fireworks Frenzy at Hunter Street Park pairs a Parade of Wheels, a drone show and fireworks; Cary, Garner and Wake Forest run their own free celebrations the same evening. Spend the day on Apex's historic Salem Street, then pick your fireworks.

morning.title: Historic Salem Street, Apex
morning.notes: Browse the shops and cafés of one of NC's best-preserved main streets before the heat peaks.

afternoon.title: Apex Fireworks Frenzy — Parade of Wheels
afternoon.location: Hunter Street Park, 1250 Ambergate Station, Apex, NC 27502
afternoon.notes: Food, games and a 4:30 PM Parade of Wheels kick off the evening at Hunter Street Park.

evening.title: Apex Drone Show + Fireworks
evening.location: Hunter Street Park, 1250 Ambergate Station, Apex, NC 27502
evening.notes: Drone show ~8:45 PM, fireworks ~9:30 PM. Prefer a big-name amphitheater crowd? Garner's Lake Benson Park has the NC Symphony + fireworks the same night.

food.vegan_dish: Oat-milk latte + vegan muffin
food.notes: Fuel on Salem St before the day.

food.vegan_dish: Ask for the veggie bowl / build a vegan plate
food.notes: Casual downtown Apex spot with rotating veg options.

food.place: Food trucks at Hunter Street Park
food.vegan_dish: Veggie taco or falafel from a lot vendor
food.notes: Eat at the celebration to hold your fireworks spot.

alternatives.leg: Where to watch fireworks on the 3rd
alternatives.rain: If Apex postpones, Garner (Lake Benson Park) and Wake Forest (Heritage High) run the same night — check town channels.
Duck into Salem St shops and cafés between showers (low storm risk on the 3rd).

practical_notes: Hot and sunny (~102°F) but a lower storm risk than midweek — still bring water and sun cover.
Arrive by dusk and park a few blocks out; Hunter Street Park parking fills fast.
A great pet/kid-friendly option: Apex adds a drone show alongside the fireworks.

itineraries.title: Bull City Sunday: Baseball, Gardens & Harry Connick Jr.
itineraries.theme: An easygoing post-holiday Sunday of gardens, ballpark fireworks and a jazz icon
itineraries.overview: Wind down the holiday weekend in Durham: a cool morning stroll through Sarah P. Duke Gardens, an afternoon Durham Bulls game with a Sunday fireworks show, and — for a dressed-up finish — an evening with Harry Connick, Jr. at DPAC. Pick the ballpark or the theater; both are a short hop from downtown.

morning.title: Sarah P. Duke Gardens
morning.location: Sarah P. Duke Gardens, 420 Anderson St, Durham
morning.notes: 55 acres of gardens; go early before the midday heat. Free admission.

afternoon.title: Durham Bulls vs. Gwinnett Stripers + Fireworks
afternoon.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham, NC 27701
afternoon.notes: First pitch 5:05 PM with a post-game fireworks show to close the homestand.

evening.title: An Evening with Harry Connick, Jr. (alternative)
evening.location: DPAC (Durham Performing Arts Center), 123 Vivian St, Durham, NC 27701
evening.notes: Prefer AC and a show? Trade the ballpark for DPAC. Or catch Madison Beer at Red Hat Amphitheater in Raleigh the same night.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan pastry + drip coffee
food.vegetarian_dish: German breakfast board with soft pretzel
food.notes: German-style bakery-café near the gardens.

food.vegan_dish: Marinated tofu & veg panino (ask to hold cheese)
food.notes: Downtown Italian sandwich shop; quick and reliable.

food.vegan_dish: Veggie-loaded nachos at the DBAP
food.notes: Eat at the game, or grab a sit-down dinner near DPAC if you swap to the show.

alternatives.rain: Slight PM storm chance — DPAC (indoors) is the dry-weather-proof choice; keep it as your backup.
The Nasher Museum (free) is a nearby indoor alternative on Duke's campus.

practical_notes: Hot (~102°F) with a slight evening storm chance — pack a light layer and check the forecast before first pitch.
Duke Gardens parking is paid; arrive early on a summer weekend.
Choose one evening anchor (Bulls or DPAC) — they overlap in time.

itineraries.title: Weeknight Arts & Ale: A Low-Key Monday in Durham
itineraries.theme: Beat the post-holiday lull with gardens, a museum and brewery trivia
itineraries.overview: A relaxed first-Monday-after-the-Fourth in Durham: free art at the Nasher, a stroll through Duke Gardens when the day cools, and a low-key evening of Geeks Who Drink trivia at Ponysaurus Brewing. Ideal if you want the Triangle without the holiday crowds.

morning.title: Nasher Museum of Art
morning.location: Nasher Museum of Art, 2001 Campus Dr, Durham
morning.notes: Free admission; the 'Tall Tales and Short Stories' exhibition is on view all summer.

afternoon.title: Sarah P. Duke Gardens (golden hour)
afternoon.location: Sarah P. Duke Gardens, 420 Anderson St, Durham
afternoon.notes: Cooler late-afternoon walk once the day's heat breaks.

evening.title: Trivia Night at Ponysaurus Brewing
evening.location: Ponysaurus Brewing Co., 219 Hood St, Durham, NC 27701
evening.notes: Geeks Who Drink trivia 6:30–8:30 PM with beer prizes; pizza and pints on the patio.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan donut + tofu scramble biscuit
food.notes: Durham breakfast staple.

food.vegan_dish: Vegetable bibimbap (no egg), add tofu
food.notes: Korean comfort food downtown; easy veg swaps.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan slice or falafel from the night's truck
food.notes: Rotating food trucks at the brewery; check ponysaurusbrewing.com for the night's vendor.

alternatives.rain: PM thunderstorms are possible Monday — swap in more Nasher time or a downtown café.
Ponysaurus has indoor seating; trivia runs regardless.

practical_notes: Hot with an afternoon/evening thunderstorm chance (~102°F high) — keep a rain plan.
The Nasher is free; Duke Gardens parking is paid.
Trivia is walk-in and free — arrive a little early to grab a table for your team.
